title: Three Weeks and One Short Tray
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：pot　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pot 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 the baker ① filled the pot that no customer in the bakery would have noted, and he said the filling was the whole of the week. The ② pot, meaning the vessel itself and not the tray, ran three weeks and stayed unnoted in the book; a pot, he said, is the only thing in a bakery that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ pot in that bakery had the same short tray beside it, and the ④ pot at the far oven, meaning the slice they kept for the children to taste and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A pot, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the baker said the noting is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the pot was the whole of the matter, meaning the share and not the vessel. The ⑥ pot, meaning the share and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; pot, he said, is either something you fill or the only word that means both a vessel and a share. He said the share is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ pot had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short tray. The ⑧ pot of the whole thing, the baker wrote in December, was one bakery and three weeks of noting; pot, he said, is either the slice at the far oven or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ pot I remember is the vessel noted in the bill, which closed in 1960 and is still noted as the quietest in the bakery. A ⑩ pot, my mother said in 1962, is the only vessel that improves by being noted; every pot, she said, is a share that has agreed to look like a vessel. She said the share was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 锅；壶（指糕饼铺里每一只旁边的那一只）
B. n. 锅；壶（指那只锅本身，与薄薄的托盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：fill the pot 盛这一只锅
D. n. 锅；壶（指留给孩子们尝的那一片）
E. n. 锅之事（抽象总称，指一处糕饼铺的锅之事）
F. n. 锅；壶（指账单里写到、被记下的那一只）
G. n. 锅、同锅（指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 同锅（抽象总称，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: filled the pot that no customer in the bakery would have noted
The pot, meaning the vessel itself and not the tray
the pot at the far oven
the pot was the whole of the matter
the pot had become a line in a bill
The pot of the whole thing
A pot, my mother said in 1962

answers.why: fill the pot 意为“盛这一只锅”，1953 年那位面点师把糕饼铺里没有一位顾客肯记下的一只锅做了一遍。
pot 意为“锅；壶”，指那只锅本身而不是薄薄的托盘，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记下。
pot 意为“锅；壶”，指糕饼铺里每一只旁边的那一只，每一只旁边都有同一只薄薄的托盘。
pot 意为“锅；壶”，指最远那座炉口的留给孩子们尝的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
pot 意为“锅、同锅”，指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这只同锅就是那件事的全部。
pot 意为“同锅”，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西而不是那只锅，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
pot 意为“锅；壶”，指账单里写到、被记下的那一只，到 1958 年这一只成了账单里的一行。
pot 意为“锅之事”，面点师十二月写道，整件事的锅之事是一处糕饼铺和三个星期的记下。
pot 意为“锅；壶”，我记得的是账单里记下过的那一只，1960 年卖完了，至今仍被说成糕饼铺里最安静的一只。
pot 为抽象总称，母亲 1962 年说，锅是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的锅。
